title: Placebo and nocebo effects on cognition: Mechanisms, mediators, and cognitive resource constraints
title_zh: 安慰剂与负安慰剂对认知的影响：机制、调节因素与认知资源限制
abstract: Placebo and nocebo effects are well established in domains such as pain and motor performance; however, their impact on cognitive functioning remains a matter of debate. This narrative review provides a state of the art on placebo and nocebo research across different cognitive domains, identifies major methodological limitations and gaps in the literature, and proposes new hypotheses to guide future research. Given the limited number of studies and the heterogeneity in experimental paradigms, cognitive outcomes, and procedures, the available evidence supports only preliminary conclusions. Some studies suggest that reward-based learning and emotional processing may be susceptible to placebo and nocebo manipulations, whereas evidence concerning memory, attention, and working memory is limited and inconclusive. Building on this synthesis, we propose that factors such as outcome measures, task-specific features, and intervention type may modulate these effects. We also hypothesize that placebo/nocebo interventions, operating through implicit (e.g., conditioning) or explicit (e.g., verbal instructions) mechanisms, may influence cognitive performance differently depending on whether expectations target cognition directly or indirectly. These hypotheses remain to be tested using controlled and directly comparable experimental designs. By highlighting gaps in the literature, this review aims to stimulate future research establishing whether placebo and nocebo effects can be reliably elicited in specific cognitive functions and clarifying how and to what extent different procedures can influence them. These lines of research could have long-term translational implications, ultimately improving the effectiveness of neuropsychological interventions and cognitive training programs that leverage positive beliefs and mitigate negative expectations.
abstract_zh: 安慰剂与负安慰剂效应在疼痛和运动表现等领域已得到充分证实；然而，它们对认知功能的影响仍存在争议。本综述对不同认知领域的安慰剂与负安慰剂研究进行了系统梳理，指出了主要方法学局限和文献空白，并提出了新的假设以指导未来研究。鉴于现有研究数量有限且实验范式、认知结果和程序高度异质，现有证据仅支持初步结论。部分研究表明基于奖励的学习和情绪加工可能易受安慰剂与负安慰剂操纵的影响，而关于记忆、注意力和工作记忆的证据有限且不确定。基于此综述，我们提出，结果测量、任务特定特征和干预类型等因素可能调节这些效应。我们还假设，安慰剂/负安慰剂干预通过隐性（如条件作用）或显性（如口头指令）机制，可能根据期望是否直接或间接针对认知而不同地影响认知表现。这些假设仍需通过受控且可直接比较的实验设计进行检验。通过突出文献中的空白，本综述旨在激发未来研究，以确定安慰剂与负安慰剂效应是否能在特定认知功能中可靠诱发，并阐明不同程序如何以及在何种程度上影响它们。这些研究方向可能具有长期的转化意义，最终提升利用正面信念和减轻负面期望的神经心理干预和认知训练项目的有效性。
